---
title: "First session in Live"
subtitle: "From an empty track to memory echoes in ten minutes"
---

You need a Live set with some audio playing in time: a drum loop, a synth part, your own playing through an
input. Anything with a few different bars works best, because memory is about recalling *similar* bars.

## 1. Load it and hear a plain delay

1. Drag **MINERVA Space Echo** (browser → Plug-Ins → CrumpLab) onto the track, after your instrument.
2. Open the preset menu at the top of the plug-in window and choose **02 Tape Delay**.
3. Press play.

You hear a 1-bar tape delay with a little feedback. That is not a coincidence: with **Memory Capacity** set to
1, memory holds exactly one bar and always answers with it, so the model reduces to a delay. This is a good
check that tempo sync and routing work.

## 2. Give it a memory

Choose **03 Memory Echo**. Memory now holds up to 100 bars. Watch the **memory matrix**
(top left): a new row appears at every bar line, oldest at the top.

![](../images/screenshot.png){fig-alt="The memory matrix fills with a row per bar."}

At each bar line the bar you just played becomes the **cue**. Every stored bar gets an **activation** (the
amber bars in the *Activation* column) by how similar it is to the cue, and the echo you hear during the next
bar is their activation-weighted blend. Each row's coloured strip is its **address**: the spectrogram-like
pattern MINERVA compares.

Play something new, then return to an earlier part: the rows from that earlier part light up again.

## 3. Hear only earlier memories

Choose **04 Deja Vu**. **Self Match** is off, so the bar you just played can't answer itself, and
**Activation Power** is 9, so only the closest earlier bars answer. It stops sounding like a delay and starts
sounding like being reminded.

Try **Activation Power** at 1 (Retrieval page): every memory contributes and the echo becomes a blurred
average of everything you've played, what Hintzman called a *schema*.

## 4. Keep what matters

- Click the **lock column** (far left) on a row to **clamp** that bar: it will never be replaced when memory is
  full.
- **Freeze Memory** (Main page) stops storing: memory keeps answering but stops learning.
- **Clear All** empties memory; **Clear Unclamped** keeps the clamped bars.

## 5. Make it a Space Echo

Choose **06 Worn Space Echo** or **21 Memory on Tape** for wow, flutter, drive and a spring tail, or
**07 Three Heads** for the RE-201's three playback heads. The *Heads* column shows which bars each head is
playing (1 amber, 2 teal, 3 violet).

## 6. Seed it

Drag an audio file (a drum break, a phrase, a field recording) onto the plug-in window. It is cut into traces of
the current length and added to memory, so what you play recalls pieces of it. See
[Importing and saving memory](../guide/import-save.qmd).
